summary.short: German Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG), described only by its table of contents. It sets rules for personal data processing by public and private bodies under the GDPR and for law enforcement under Directive (EU) 2016/680, and creates a Federal Data Protection Commissioner.
summary.long: The Bundesdatenschutzgesetz (BDSG) is known here only from its unofficial table of contents; no operative provision text is in the document, and the outline gives no date of entry into force. Part 1 (common provisions) covers scope and definitions, processing by public bodies, video surveillance of publicly accessible spaces, data protection officers of public bodies, and the Federal Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information with its powers, reports and cooperation, plus judicial remedies. Part 2 implements processing rules for the purposes of Article 2 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679, covering special categories and further processing, employment, research, archiving, consumer credit, scoring, data subject rights including automated individual decisions, controller and processor duties, state supervisory authorities, fines, criminal provisions and court remedies. Part 3 implements Directive (EU) 2016/680 for law enforcement, with principles, legal bases, data subject rights, duties of controllers and processors, breach notification, impact assessments, third-country transfers, liability and penalties. Part 4 covers processing outside the scope of EU law and processing for state honours.

notes: The document is the unofficial table of contents (nichtamtliches Inhaltsverzeichnis) of the BDSG from gesetze-im-internet.de. It contains headings only, no operative provisions, so no obligations, thresholds, enforcement, definitions, events or classifications could be coded. Relations and entities come from headings only. The enabling act, amended acts and the 30 June 2017 date are not in the document (the date comes from registry metadata). The Part 4 heading covers activities outside both the GDPR and the Directive 2016/680, so it is a scope reference to both and is not coded as a separate relation. Full text is needed for legal_basis, amendment relations and the operative entities.
